lesson.title: The Register Ladder Recap
lesson.subtitle: Walking the 9 conversion bridges from English formal register into everyday French.

hook.title: Walking All Nine Conversion Bridges in One Circuit
hook.content: Review all 9 conversion bridges that connect your formal English vocabulary directly to French: -ion, -ation→-er, -ité, -ance/-ence, -ed↔-é, -ly→-ment, -or→-eur, -able/-ible, and Norman Doublets!

footnotes.title: How one Latin root rides across four bridges at once
footnotes.content: Take 'possible / différ-': la possibilité (-ité), possible (-ible), la différence (-ence), différemment (-ment) — one root, four bridges!

pattern.title: See the English Suffix, Fire the French Bridge
pattern.content: Run a rapid synthesis across all nine conversion families.
pattern.linguist_note: Shared Latin-Norman derivational suffixes account for over 65% of shared English-French lexical density.
pattern.trap_note: Remember the gender locks: -ion, -ité, -ance, -ence are 100% feminine (la/une)!

exercises.prompt: Match each conversion bridge with its rule and gender lock:
exercises.target_answer: 100% Feminine nouns, 100% Feminine nouns, Active infinitive verbs, Manner adverbs, Gender-invariable adjectives
exercises.meaning: -ion & -ité (la tradition, la liberté), -ance & -ence (l'importance, la patience), -ation → -er (organiser, célébrer), -ly → feminine + -ment (naturellement), -able / -ible (capable, visible)
exercises.explanation: Nine bridges unlock thousands of French words from English you already know.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence below uses four conversion bridges at once without a single error?
options: Naturelment, c'est une décision possible à l'université
Naturellement, c'est un décision possible à le université
Naturellement, c'est une décision possible à l'université
exercises.target_answer: Naturellement, c'est une décision possible à l'université
exercises.meaning: Naturally (-ment), it is a possible (-ible) decision (-ion, f.) at the university (-ité, elided)
exercises.explanation: naturelle + ment, feminine une décision, invariable possible, and elided l'université.

exercises.prompt: Convert the English phrase 'really impossible' using the -ment and -ible bridges:

exercises.idea: fortunately it is possible to confirm the reservation
cues: it is possible to confirm → c'est possible de confirmer
idea_parts: pointer + adjective + verb → c'est possible de confirmer
exercises.target_answer: Heureusement, c'est possible de confirmer la réservation
exercises.meaning: Fortunately, it is possible to confirm the reservation

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: Le directeur a confirmé la décision immédiatement
exercises.target_answer: Le directeur a confirmé la décision immédiatement
exercises.meaning: The director confirmed the decision immediately
exercises.explanation: Four bridges in one natural sentence!

summary.outcome: Synthesize all 9 conversion bridges across nouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs.

use_example.german: Finalement, l'organisation a confirmé la possibilité.
use_example.english: Finally, the organization confirmed the possibility.

summary.takeaway: Nine suffix bridges turn your English vocabulary into a live French lexicon.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on Le Pont ([2903] Spoken French Shortcuts): see how The Register Ladder Recap leads directly into Spoken French Shortcuts.

twist.prompt: Think it through again without looking back — express "Fortunately, it is possible to confirm the reservation" in French:
twist.target_answer: Heureusement, c'est possible de confirmer la réservation
twist.explanation: Re-constructing "Heureusement, c'est possible de confirmer la réservation" from the underlying rule cements the pattern of The Register Ladder Recap.

confirmation.etymology_derivation: The nasal N is thought, not said: confiRmation with the N half-swallowed.

confirmer.etymology_derivation: confirmation → confirmer. Strip -ation, bolt on -er (pronounced /e/), and the noun becomes the verb.

université.etymology_derivation: -ity → -ité, and every -ité is feminine. The accent on the é marks the final syllable English swallows.

différence.etymology_derivation: Latin differentia. The -ance/-ence endings convert whole and are always feminine.

docteur.etymology_derivation: Latin doctor 'teacher'. -or/-er nouns convert to -eur and are usually masculine.

hôtel.shift_rule: Norman doublet: S and H dropped
hôtel.etymology_derivation: Latin hospitalis → hostel AND hôtel — the same word entered English twice: once with its S (hostel, hospital), once without (hôtel).

mangé.etymology_derivation: manger ← Latin manducāre 'to chew'. English 'mange' is the eating disease — the verb came with the Normans' dogs.
